I've been working this same flat land in Quzhou for over thirty years, same as my father before me. I know this soil, I know what sells at the grain station, and I know what my neighbors grow. There is no reason to change what works.

My land is about 10 mu, all of it irrigated with the groundwater pump we share with three other families. The plot is flat and easy to work with the small rototiller I rent from the cooperative each season.

I will grow winter wheat this autumn and follow it with summer maize after the June harvest — the same rotation I have done every year. Everyone in the village does this. The grain station buys both, the inputs are available at the agro-supply shop in town, and I know exactly when and how much to apply.

For the wheat I will use Jimai 22 — I have been planting this variety for six or seven years and it has never failed me badly. I will rotary-till before sowing and apply compound fertilizer as base, then top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate four times: at sowing to get germination, at overwintering, at jointing, and at heading. I spray twice — once for weeds in late autumn and once for aphids and rust before heading.

For the maize I plant hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 usually, right into the wheat stubble without ploughing to save time and diesel money. Summer rain usually handles most of the water, but I pump twice if it is dry at tasseling. I top-dress urea once at the 8-leaf stage.

I expect around 450 jin per mu for wheat and 550 for maize. Nothing spectacular, but reliable.
